subject: Vocabulary
description: Greek root PHIL (love) — philosophy, philanthropy, philharmonic, bibliophile, francophile, philately, hemophilia.

questions.stem: PHIL root means 'love'. PHILANTHROPY literally means:
questions.explanation: PHILANTHROPY — etymology PHIL (love) + ANTHROPOS (human, Greek) = 'LOVE OF HUMANITY' = practice of donating money/time/effort to benefit other people, esp. through charity. WORD FAMILY (root PHIL = love, friend, fond): (1) PHILOSOPHY — 'love of wisdom' (philo + sophia). (2) PHILANTHROPY — 'love of humanity'. (3) PHILHARMONIC — 'love of harmony' (orchestra name, e.g., New York Philharmonic). (4) BIBLIOPHILE — 'lover of books'. (5) FRANCOPHILE — 'lover of French (culture)'. (6) ANGLOPHILE — 'lover of England'. (7) AUDIOPHILE — 'lover of high-fidelity audio'. (8) CINEPHILE — 'lover of cinema'. (9) PHILATELY — 'love of stamps' (philos + ateleia 'tax-free'); stamp collecting. (10) PHILANDERER — 'lover of (many) men/women' (negative, often a person who has many love affairs). MEDICAL: HEMOPHILIA = 'love of blood' (a misnomer; means tendency to bleed; X-linked recessive disorder; affected Russian Tsar's son Alexei). FAMOUS PHILANTHROPISTS: Andrew Carnegie, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Azim Premji (India — Wipro), Ratan Tata (Tata Trusts). INDIAN context: Tata's ~66% wealth in TRUSTS for charity. PYQ FREQUENCY: PHIL root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, IBPS PO English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: PHILOSOPHY — etymology PHILOS (love) + SOPHIA (wisdom, knowledge) = 'LOVE OF WISDOM'. Coined by PYTHAGORAS (~570-495 BCE), who described himself as a 'philosopher' (lover of wisdom) — modest compared to claiming to BE wise. BRANCHES: (1) METAPHYSICS — nature of reality, existence. (2) EPISTEMOLOGY — theory of knowledge. (3) ETHICS — moral philosophy. (4) LOGIC — valid reasoning. (5) AESTHETICS — beauty, art. (6) POLITICAL philosophy — state, justice. (7) PHILOSOPHY OF MIND, language, science. KEY GREEK PHILOSOPHERS: Socrates (~470-399 BCE, 'know thyself'), Plato (~427-347 BCE, founded the Academy), Aristotle (~384-322 BCE, founded Lyceum + tutored Alexander). INDIAN PHILOSOPHY: 6 ASTIKA (orthodox) schools — Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, Vedanta. NASTIKA (heterodox) — Charvaka, Jainism, Buddhism. KEY THINKERS: Adi Shankaracharya (Advaita), Ramanujacharya (Vishishtadvaita), Madhvacharya (Dvaita). WESTERN MODERN: Descartes ('I think therefore I am'), Kant, Hegel, Nietzsche, Russell, Wittgenstein. SOPHIA root: SOPHISTICATED, SOPHIST, SOPHOMORE (Greek 'sophos'). WORDS WITH SOPHIA: PHILOSOPHY (lover of wisdom), THEOSOPHY (divine wisdom), SOPHIST (wise person, often pejorative), SOPHISTRY (clever but misleading reasoning). PYQ FREQUENCY: philosophy etymology in CAT, GRE, advanced IBPS PO 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A BIBLIOPHILE is someone who loves:
questions.explanation: BIBLIOPHILE — etymology BIBLIO (book, Greek) + PHIL (love) = 'BOOK LOVER'. Often refers to those who collect rare/antique books, but generally means anyone with deep love of books. BIBLIO ROOT WORDS: (1) BIBLIOGRAPHY — list of books cited. (2) BIBLIOTHECA — library (Latin term used in some libraries' names). (3) BIBLE — 'the book' (THE book in Christian context). (4) BIBLIOPHOBIA — fear of books. (5) BIBLIOMANIA — obsessive book collection. WORLD-CLASS BIBLIOPHILES: J.P. Morgan (Pierpont Morgan Library, NY); Sir Thomas Phillipps (collected 60,000+ books, 19th c.); Umberto Eco (~50,000 books). FAMOUS LIBRARIES: (a) Library of Congress (Washington, ~170 million items). (b) British Library (London, ~170 million). (c) Bibliothèque Nationale de France (Paris, ~40 million). (d) Vatican Library. (e) BHANDARKAR ORIENTAL Research Institute (Pune, India — major Sanskrit-manuscript collection). (f) ASIATIC SOCIETY OF BENGAL (Kolkata). RELATED -PHILE WORDS: (1) AUDIOPHILE (sound). (2) OENOPHILE (wine). (3) FOODIE (food, informal). (4) CINEPHILE (cinema). (5) DENDROPHILE (trees). PYQ FREQUENCY: BIBLIOPHILE in SSC CGL, CAT, IBPS PO 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: PHILATELY is the hobby of collecting:
questions.explanation: PHILATELY — etymology PHIL (love) + ATELEIA (Greek, 'tax-free' or 'exempt from payment') = 'love of (things signifying) tax-free' — referring to PRE-PAID postage. Modern meaning: STAMP COLLECTING + study. ORIGIN: term coined 1864 by Frenchman Georges Herpin. ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION: stamps mean the recipient doesn't pay (tax-free for them). HOBBY OVERVIEW: most popular collectible globally — 200+ million collectors worldwide; ~30 million in India. KEY ASPECTS: (1) ACCUMULATING stamps. (2) Studying RARITY, history, design. (3) Trading at auctions. INDIA — KEY STAMPS: First Indian stamp = 'Scinde Dawk' (1852, ~₹500 face but rare; original sells for lakhs). Modern stamps: Mahatma Gandhi (1948 series, very valuable in mint condition). VALUABLE WORLD STAMPS: (a) British Guiana 1c Magenta (1856) — sold $9.5M (2014); world's most valuable. (b) Treskilling Yellow (Sweden, 1855). KEY BODIES: (a) PHILATELIC SOCIETY of INDIA. (b) Philatelic Bureaus at India Post. (c) WORLD STAMP exhibitions (e.g., London Stamp Festival). RELATED COLLECTING HOBBIES: NUMISMATICS (coins), DELTIOLOGY (postcards), VEXILLOLOGY (flags). PYQ FREQUENCY: philately definition in SSC CGL, CAT vocabulary 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: HEMOPHILIA is a medical condition involving:
questions.explanation: HEMOPHILIA — genetic disorder where blood DOES NOT CLOT properly due to deficiency of clotting factor (Factor VIII for Hemophilia A; Factor IX for Hemophilia B). NAME: HEMO (blood) + PHILIA (love/affinity) = 'love of blood' — historically a misnomer (does NOT mean 'love of blood'; rather 'tendency for blood to leak'). SYMPTOMS: prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, spontaneous internal bleeding (esp. joints — 'haemarthrosis'), easy bruising. INHERITANCE: X-LINKED RECESSIVE — gene on X chromosome. Mostly affects MALES (single X). FEMALES are usually CARRIERS (pass to sons). FAMOUS CASE: ALEXEI ROMANOV (1904-1918), youngest son of Tsar Nicholas II of Russia, had severe hemophilia. His mother Alexandra invited Rasputin to treat him; Rasputin's influence at the court contributed to political destabilization → Russian Revolution 1917 → execution of Romanovs. QUEEN VICTORIA was a CARRIER; passed gene to many European royal families ('royal disease'). TREATMENT: clotting-factor replacement therapy (recombinant or plasma-derived); prophylactic injections; new gene therapies emerging (2024). PYQ FREQUENCY: hemophilia in NEET, AIIMS, SSC GA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: An AUDIOPHILE is a person who loves:
questions.explanation: AUDIOPHILE — etymology AUDIO (Latin 'audire' = to hear) + PHIL (love) = 'lover of high-quality SOUND/audio'. Hobbyist who pursues audio reproduction at the highest fidelity, often investing in: (1) High-end SPEAKERS (Bose, B&W, KEF, Wilson Audio). (2) High-end AMPLIFIERS (McIntosh, Marantz). (3) TURNTABLES + vinyl records (analog, prized for warmth). (4) HEADPHONES (Sennheiser HD 800, Audeze, Stax — can cost $5,000+). (5) DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converters). MUSIC FORMATS preferred: VINYL records, HIGH-RES DIGITAL (FLAC, DSD), SACD. AVOIDED: low-bitrate MP3, compressed streaming. AUDIOPHILE COMMUNITY: 1000s of forums, Reddit (/r/audiophile), high-end audio shows. CRITICISM: some claims (e.g., gold-plated cables improve sound) are scientifically disputed (PLACEBO effect studies, blind tests often find no difference). VALUE PROPOSITION: 'good enough' vs 'last 5% perfection' — diminishing returns. NAMES: 'budget audiophile' vs 'high-end audiophile'. INDIA: bustling audio-enthusiast scene in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai. RELATED words: VIDEOPHILE (high-quality video), CINEPHILE (cinema lover). PYQ FREQUENCY: audiophile + similar -phile words in CAT, IBPS PO English 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: FRANCOPHILE describes a person with strong affinity for:
questions.explanation: FRANCOPHILE — etymology FRANCO (relating to France) + PHIL (love) = 'lover of France/French culture'. May have love for French language, cuisine, fashion, art, history. OPPOSITES: FRANCOPHOBE — disdain for France. RELATED NATION-WORDS with PHIL/PHOBE: (1) ANGLOPHILE — love of England (Anglophobe = dislike). (2) AMERICOPHILE — love of America. (3) GERMANOPHILE — Germany. (4) RUSSOPHILE — Russia. (5) HISPANOPHILE — Spain. (6) NIPPOPHILE — Japan. (7) SINOPHILE — China (sino = Chinese). (8) INDOPHILE — love of India. NOTABLE Francophiles: Thomas Jefferson (US founding father, served as ambassador to France); Hemingway, James Joyce (lived in Paris); recent celebrities living in France for tax+culture. INDIA — FRANCO-INDIAN connection: French East India Company; PONDICHERRY (Puducherry) was French until 1954; CHANDERNAGORE, KARIKAL etc. were French enclaves. ALLIANCE FRANÇAISE has 16 centers in India promoting French language/culture. ACADEMIC: 'Francophilia' in 18th-19th century Europe — French was prestige language; aristocrats spoke French. PYQ FREQUENCY: -phile/-phobe word pairs in CAT, GRE, advanced IBPS PO English 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests advanced cultural-vocabulary breadth.
